ncd1e2944b3b.s: The first Visalandhra Mahasabha at Warangal demanded that Hyderabad State be divided into three linguistic parts, with ____ as the capital.
ncd1e2944b3b.x: The first Mahasabha called for Hyderabad as the capital and for Hyderabad State to be divided into three linguistic parts.

n09c7f6cdab0.s: The Congress was initially cold towards the Visalandhra proposal mainly because the idea had been advanced by the:
n09c7f6cdab0.x: The idea came from the Communists, and the Congress feared a united state might give them a majority.

n58a7d55ddc5.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nehru announced the SRC in the Lok Sabha – 29 December 1953
Report of the States Reorganisation Commission – 1955
n58a7d55ddc5.x: The SRC report came in 1955. Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953, it was constituted on 29 December 1953, and the Mahasabha was founded in 1949.

nap-history-27-6.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: N.G. Ranga – First President of the Andhra Socialist Party
Nadendla Bhaskara Rao – President of the Telangana Praja Samithi
Marri Chenna Reddy – President of the Telangana Praja Samithi
Communist Party – Initiated the Visalandhra Movement
nap-history-27-6.x: Nadendla Bhaskara Rao formed the Democratic Telugu Desam Party; it was Marri Chenna Reddy who led the Telangana Praja Samithi.

n4edb7d8af2d.s: In 1954, B. Ramakrishna Rao changed his earlier stand and advocated:
o: Continuation of Hyderabad as a multilingual State
Early merger of Telangana with Andhra
n4edb7d8af2d.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao, who had initially backed a separate Telangana, changed his position in 1954 and advocated early merger of Telangana with Andhra.

n7e9d4183c52.s: Regarding the Hyderabad Congress, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: June 1953 – Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
8 July 1954 – Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC
November 1955 – Resolution for dividing Hyderabad State into three parts
1954 – Telangana convention backed a separate Telangana
n7e9d4183c52.x: The Hyderabad PCC delegation met the SRC on 8 July 1954. The three-part resolution was of June 1953 and was rejected in 1954; separate Telangana was backed in November 1955.

nccf22ab2b78.s: The argument that Telangana could exist as a separate State rested on its higher ____ compared with Andhra State.
nccf22ab2b78.x: Telangana's higher per capita income and revenue than Andhra State made it economically viable on its own.

n36e50d421f2.s: Under paragraph 386 of the SRC report, Telangana could merge with Andhra after the 1961 elections only if its legislature approved it by a:
n36e50d421f2.x: The SRC recommended a separate Telangana initially, with merger after the 1961 elections only on a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature.

nae1a92e3420.s: The dismissal of N.T. Rama Rao's government in 1984 is a textbook example of the alleged misuse of the discretion of the:
nae1a92e3420.x: The 1984 dismissal is cited as a classic misuse of gubernatorial discretion and fed into the later Sarkaria Commission debates.

ncd214b9257e.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 adapted the model of which earlier pact for settling regional apprehensions?
ncd214b9257e.x: Like the Sribagh Pact, the Gentlemen's Agreement addressed regional fears through a moral and political understanding rather than a constitutional settlement.

n166c9cd81c6.s: How many leaders signed the Gentlemen's Agreement of 20 February 1956?
n166c9cd81c6.x: Eight leaders signed it, four from Andhra and four from Telangana.

n069968df0eb.s: Under the Gentlemen's Agreement, Telangana students were assured admission priority or at least ____ of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.
n069968df0eb.x: The agreement gave Telangana students admission priority or at least one-third of the seats in technical institutions, whichever was more favourable.

nd14fb20ca11.s: The 1957 Assembly elections in Andhra Pradesh were held only in Telangana, covering how many seats?
nd14fb20ca11.x: The 1957 elections were held only in Telangana and covered 79 seats.

ne876b535e1e.s: The 1984 NTR–Nadendla Bhaskara Rao crisis contributed to the anti-defection law enacted through the:
ne876b535e1e.x: The episode contributed to the anti-defection law enacted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment, 1985.

nb90f4c78d9a.s: Which of the following pairs (leader – national office) is correctly matched?
o: P.V. Narasimha Rao – Chairman, National Front
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy – Prime Minister of India
nb90f4c78d9a.x: Damodaram Sanjivayya was AICC President. Sanjiva Reddy was President of India, P.V. Narasimha Rao Prime Minister and NTR Chairman of the National Front.

nedb3308cc9e.s: Who is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, with N. Chandrababu Naidu as Chief Minister and Amaravati as capital?
nedb3308cc9e.x: S. Abdul Nazeer is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, whose capital is Amaravati and Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

nap-history-25-10.s: The Join Indian Union Movement in Hyderabad was launched on:
nap-history-25-10.x: It began on 7 August 1947 against the Nizam's plan to keep Hyderabad independent; 17 September 1948 is the date of integration after Operation Polo.

ndf71f80a1fc.x: Dasarathi wrote 'Enni Naalla Swapnamidi', while Kaloji wrote 'Emaanandam ... Eenadu'.

nc64b327d41c.s: The Mandal system of local administration was introduced in Andhra Pradesh by the NTR government from:
nc64b327d41c.x: NTR introduced the Mandal system from 1985; in 1983 he allowed a simple majority for no-confidence motions against Zilla Parishad vice-chairmen.

nb5ccf3c27af.s: Under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, Chandigarh became:
o: A Union Territory and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana
nb5ccf3c27af.x: The 1966 Act created Punjab and Haryana and made Chandigarh a Union Territory serving as their shared capital.

n61557c48ea1.s: Which of the following pairs (State – basis of formation) is INCORRECTLY matched?
n61557c48ea1.x: Uttarakhand was formed on grounds of regional backwardness/administration, not on a linguistic basis.

ne7e26de1dc0.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Eleventh Schedule – Coal, oil, gas and power
Twelfth Schedule – Public sector undertakings and corporations
ne7e26de1dc0.x: The Tenth Schedule covers State institutions; the Ninth covers PSUs, the Eleventh irrigation projects and the Twelfth coal, oil, gas and power.

n62826a23f2c.s: A major criticism of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 is that it was passed without the consent of the:
n62826a23f2c.x: The Act was passed without the consent of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.

na6d89196153.s: The Nizam's Mulki rules required how many years of continuous residence?
na6d89196153.x: The Nizam's rules required 15 years' continuous residence, whereas the 1956 Gentlemen's Agreement suggested 12 years.

n52e631637b8.s: Who was the president of the Telangana Praja Samiti?
n52e631637b8.x: Marri Channa Reddy was president of the Telangana Praja Samiti; B. Satyanarayana Reddy later led the Complete Telangana Praja Samiti.

neca7af0ab57.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, existing admission quotas under Article 371D were continued for:
neca7af0ab57.x: The Act continued the existing Article 371D admission quotas for ten years and extended Article 371D to Telangana.

n870fdef797c.s: The Committee on Telangana (2010), which gave six options in its report, was chaired by:
n870fdef797c.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the 2010 Committee, which reported on 30 December 2010 with six options.

n41f96fb6a45.s: Who founded the Gorkha National Liberation Front and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'?
n41f96fb6a45.x: Subhash Ghisingh founded the GNLF in 1980 and coined the term 'Gorkhaland'.

n924063fb261.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lalit Committee – Legal opinion on the validity of job safeguards
Wanchoo Committee – Official accounting of surplus funds
Bhargava Committee – Legal opinion on the validity of job safeguards
Bhargava Committee – Assessment of Telangana's revenue surpluses
n924063fb261.x: The Bhargava Committee assessed Telangana's revenue surpluses; the Lalit Committee did the official accounting and the Wanchoo Committee examined job safeguards.

n92467ac49ff.s: The President gave assent to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 on:
n92467ac49ff.x: Assent was given on 1 March 2014; the appointed day, when Telangana was formed, was 2 June 2014.

naa3a494c17b.s: Regarding the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sections 84–85 – Polavaram as a national project
Section 46 – Finance Commission award, grants and backward-area package
Section 90 – Polavaram as a national project
naa3a494c17b.x: Sections 84–85 provide for the Apex Council and the River Management Boards; Polavaram is under Section 90.

n0cfe216f826.s: How many Assembly seats were initially allocated to Telangana under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014?
n0cfe216f826.x: Telangana got 119 seats and Andhra Pradesh 175; 225 and 153 are the proposed future increases under Section 26.

ne95f61c48b8.s: Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the:
ne95f61c48b8.x: It was an assurance given by the Prime Minister in the Rajya Sabha and was not a provision of the Reorganisation Act.

n2ce6b07db0c.s: Which Part of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with the formation of Telangana, the common capital and the common Governor?
n2ce6b07db0c.x: Part II (Sections 3-11) covers the reorganisation itself; Part I is preliminary, Part VI deals with assets and liabilities and Part XII with legal and miscellaneous provisions.

n37cdefa0ab8.s: The Polavaram project, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy, was originally known as:
n37cdefa0ab8.x: The original name was Ramapada Sagaram, proposed by Sir Shonthi Venkataramamurthy.

ne2dd9a368b2.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CPI (Maoist) – Charu Majumdar with Kanu Sanyal
AP extremist CPI(ML) wing – Merger of PWG and MCC
ne2dd9a368b2.x: The PWG was founded by Kondapalli Seetharamaiah; CPI(ML) is linked to Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal, and CPI (Maoist) to the PWG–MCC merger.

nc4e1da80c33.s: Who were the founding vice-presidents of Virasam?
o: Sri Sri and Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao
Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry
nc4e1da80c33.x: Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao and Rachakonda Viswanatha Sastry were the founding vice-presidents; Sri Sri was president.

nf86b15b7d68.s: The first meeting of Virasam was held in 1970 at:
nf86b15b7d68.x: The first Virasam meeting was held at Khammam in 1970.

n76179c5a70f.s: Besides Virasam, the Srikakulam movement reshaped Telugu culture through which troupe?
n76179c5a70f.x: Srikakulam made AP a core base of Indian Maoism and influenced Telugu literature through Virasam and Jana Natya Mandali.

ne59c05c6300.s: The Greyhounds, raised in 1989, is an elite anti-Naxal force of the:
ne59c05c6300.x: Greyhounds is an elite anti-Naxal special police force of the Andhra Pradesh Police, raised in 1989.

nf0df4eff353.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, primarily:
o: Procures minor forest produce and supplies essentials to tribals
nf0df4eff353.x: The GCC procures minor forest produce and supplies essential goods, freeing tribals from moneylenders.

n0ff97d5c6bb.s: Who founded the Andhra Pradesh Dalit Mahasabha in 1985, after Karamchedu?
n0ff97d5c6bb.x: Katti Padmarao is identified as its founder, with Bojja Tarakam also recognised as a founder.

na933ed147c6.s:
Regarding Bhu Poratam:
1. It was jointly launched by the CPI and CPI(M) in Andhra Pradesh.
2. It was launched in 1997.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
na933ed147c6.x: Bhu Poratam was a joint CPI–CPI(M) land struggle, but it was launched in 2007, not 1997.

nfabed0e711e.s: The first Andhra Pradesh Backward Class Commission, which grouped BCs into A–D categories, was the:
nfabed0e711e.x: The Anantharaman Commission (1968–70) was the first AP Backward Class Commission and grouped BCs into A–D categories.

n6c6908457ac.s: Following Muthulakshmi Reddy's campaign, Ammannaraja moved an anti-dedication (Devadasi) bill in the Madras Assembly in:
n6c6908457ac.x: Ammannaraja's anti-dedication bill came in the Madras Assembly in 1937, after Muthulakshmi Reddy's campaign.

n035d367743e.s: Which of the following newspaper – founder pairs is correctly matched?
n035d367743e.x: Udayam was founded by Dasari Narayana Rao; Andhra Jyothi by K.L.N. Prasad, Eenadu by Ramoji Rao and Sakshi by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.

n8297aa2823d.s: The Nandi Awards of the Andhra Pradesh Government for films, television and drama were instituted in:
n8297aa2823d.x: Nandi Awards are AP Government awards for films, television and drama, instituted in 1964.

nc7a726c5680.s: Firdausi, a poem about a Persian poet cheated of his promised reward by Sultan Mahmud, was written by:
nc7a726c5680.x: Firdausi is Jashuva's poem on the Persian poet cheated by Sultan Mahmud, presented as a rebel against patronage.

n5d4d4579f9d.s: Post-1956 Telugu literature shifted its focus from classical and romantic themes towards:
o: Caste, class, gender and minority identity
n5d4d4579f9d.x: Post-1956 Telugu literary streams broadened literature to take in caste, class, gender and minority identity.

n1bbc28f5f75.s: Viswanatha Satyanarayana, author of over 100 works, was known as:
n1bbc28f5f75.x: Viswanatha Satyanarayana was known as 'Abhinava Nannaya' and wrote over 100 works.

n94d71b1d0b5.s: The Nandi Awards of the Andhra Pradesh Government are given in the fields of:
n94d71b1d0b5.x: The Nandi Awards cover films, television and drama, including the Nandi Natakotsavam for drama.

n54faae35881.s: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, instituted in 1969?
n54faae35881.x: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969 and Devika Rani was its first recipient.

n6d94f599446.s: The Nandi Awards were instituted in 1964 by:
n6d94f599446.x: The Nandi Awards were instituted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 1964; NFDC administers the National Film Awards.

n409b6819099.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gemini TV and ETV, private Telugu satellite channels, both began in 1995.
2. ETV was founded by N.T. Rama Rao.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n409b6819099.x: Both channels began in 1995, but ETV was founded by Ramoji Rao, not N.T. Rama Rao.

nb7fb3582c71.s: K. Pawan Kalyan, who became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, leads which party?
nb7fb3582c71.x: K. Pawan Kalyan is associated with the Jana Sena Party and became Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.

nf66c31cd40d.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Damerla Rama Rao – Author of Himabindu
Adivi Bapiraju – Painter, poet and novelist
nf66c31cd40d.x: Adivi Bapiraju was a painter, poet and novelist (Himabindu); Papaiah illustrated Chandamama covers and Bapu was the film director.

n5fdb99d3774.s: The AP Department of Archaeology and Museums traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department, established in:
n5fdb99d3774.x: It traces its origin to the Hyderabad State Archaeological Department of 1914; 1861 is the founding of the ASI.

n4f180a44005.s: The Archaeological Survey of India was founded in 1861 by:
n4f180a44005.x: Alexander Cunningham founded the ASI in 1861; Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda (1926) and Longhurst dug it (1927).

n4a0ed206dc9.s: Monuments at Anupu and on Nagarjunakonda island were rebuilt on higher ground because of submergence by the:
n4a0ed206dc9.x: The area was submerged after 1960 by the Nagarjunasagar Dam, so the ASI dismantled and rebuilt the monuments ('transplantation of monuments').

nd66f1d7270f.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gudiwada Dibba – Tara bronzes and Buddha footprint
Salihundam – Monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra
Gudiwada Dibba – Monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra
Bojjannakonda – Monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra
nd66f1d7270f.x: Bojjannakonda has a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra; Tara bronzes and a Buddha footprint belong to Salihundam, and Gudiwada Dibba has Mauryan-to-Satavahana remains.

n4b9c7d795d3.s: The Salar Jung Museum, Hyderabad, houses the collection of:
o: Mir Osman Ali Khan, Nizam VII
Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III
Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, Nizam VI
Mir Turab Ali Khan, Salar Jung I
n4b9c7d795d3.x: The museum holds the collection gathered over 40 years by Nawab Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, Salar Jung III.

n395e6fb2b49.s: Which museum is chiefly associated with the Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculpture of the Amaravati School?
n395e6fb2b49.x: The Amaravati site museum is associated with the Amaravati Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculptures of the Amaravati School.

n01b4cadd17a.s: Which land reform brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State?
n01b4cadd17a.x: Abolition of intermediaries, regarded as the most successful reform, brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.

n162d85bbba8.s: After the abolition of intermediaries in Telangana, Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became:
n162d85bbba8.x: Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.

n23838128630.s: Which of the following scheme – Chief Minister – year sets is correctly matched?
o: Rs 2 per kg rice scheme – N.T. Rama Rao – 1983
n23838128630.x: The Rs 2 per kg rice scheme, with subsidised housing and Janata cloth, was introduced by N.T. Rama Rao in 1983.

n20464331d0f.s: A major limitation of the abolition of zamindari and jagirdari was that it:
o: Changed the revenue hierarchy but left tenancy and landholding inequalities
n20464331d0f.x: Abolition mainly altered the revenue hierarchy; it did not by itself resolve tenancy problems and unequal landholding.

ned2ba7175a5.s: The formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel, under Nehru's influence, is credited to:
ned2ba7175a5.x: The Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin, under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.

nd956019e7ed.s: Who described a tribe as a 'segmental organisation' of equivalent multi-family groups?
nd956019e7ed.x: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent multi-family groups.

n950aabf43d8.s: Regarding Chenchu village offices and clans, which pair is correctly matched?
n950aabf43d8.x: Raju is associated with the Bhoomani clan; Mantri with Kumakula, and Kolagadu with the Dasari, Uttaluri or Mandla clans.

n34949a24a6c.s: Chenchu social organisation is best described as:
n34949a24a6c.x: The Chenchus are an endogamous tribe with exogamous clans (kulams/gothrams); they are patriarchal and patrilineal.

ne52028a684c.s: The agency economy of the Araku belt rests on:
o: Tea plantations, jute mills and inland shipping
Podu, minor forest produce, coffee and horticulture
Marine fishing, salt production and shipbuilding
ne52028a684c.x: The agency economy combines podu (shifting cultivation) and minor forest produce with coffee and horticulture in the Araku belt.

n6bb285c5991.s: Modakondamma, in whose honour an annual tribal jatara is held, is the goddess of the:
n6bb285c5991.x: Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of the Paderu agency, where an annual tribal jatara is held.

n0ef8381318b.s:
Consider the following pairs (dance – community):
1. Kommu – Koya
2. Gussadi – Lambada
3. Lambadi dance – Lambada/Sugali women
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
n0ef8381318b.x: Kommu is the Koya dance and the Lambadi dance is by Lambada/Sugali women; Gussadi is a Gond dance.

n2b97c855fef.s: Who led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 in the Eastern Ghats?
n2b97c855fef.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion in the Eastern Ghats from 1922 to 1924.

nc5f865c7b15.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Pitt's India Act
2. Charter Act of 1793
3. Regulating Act
4. Charter Act of 1813
nc5f865c7b15.x: Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784, Charter Act 1793, Charter Act 1813.

nf71f69358a2.s: The British Parliament intervened in the Company's affairs in Bengal in 1772 mainly because of:
o: The famine, falling revenue and the Company's financial crisis
The Carnatic Wars and the Mysore conflict
The appointment of the first Viceroy
The transfer of Bombay and Madras to Parliament
nf71f69358a2.x: The Bengal famine, declining revenue and the Company's financial crisis compelled Parliament to intervene in 1772.

nd476f5e723d.s:
Under the Indian Councils Act, 1892, recommendations for nomination came from which of the following?
1. Universities
2. Municipalities
3. Chambers of commerce
Which of the above is/are correct?
nd476f5e723d.x: The 1892 Act's indirect system worked through recommendations from universities, municipalities and chambers of commerce.

nac3228e7d4c.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. First Governor-General of Bengal – Warren Hastings
2. First Governor-General of India – Lord Canning
3. Last Viceroy of India – Lord Mountbatten
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
nac3228e7d4c.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct; the first Governor-General of India was William Bentinck, while Canning was the first Viceroy.

nindian-polity-22-5.s: Which of the following about the Charter Act, 1813 is INCORRECT?
o: It permitted Christian missionaries to work in India.
It completely abolished the Company's trade monopoly in India.
It retained the Company's monopoly over the tea and China trade.
It provided an annual grant of ₹1 lakh for education.
nindian-polity-22-5.x: The 1813 Act ended the Company's monopoly only partly, keeping the tea and China trade; complete abolition came in 1833.

nindian-polity-22-18.s:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act, 1773:
1. It banned private trade by Company officials.
2. It banned the acceptance of bribes by Company officials.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-22-18.x: The Regulating Act banned both private trade and bribes by Company officials.

nindian-polity-22-51.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian High Courts Act was passed in 1861.
2. The High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up in 1862.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-22-51.x: The Indian High Courts Act was passed in 1861, and the High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were set up under it in 1862.

nindian-polity-43-16.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Councils Act, 1861 restored the legislative powers of Bombay and Madras.
2. The 1861 Act brought the portfolio system and the Viceroy's ordinance power.
3. The Indian Councils Act, 1892 introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-43-16.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; separate electorates came with the 1909 Act, not 1892.

n75af0835a86.s: At the time of the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), Morley and Minto respectively were:
o: Governor of Bombay and Secretary of State
Secretary of State and Governor of Bengal
n75af0835a86.x: John Morley was Secretary of State for India and Lord Minto was the Viceroy when the Indian Councils Act, 1909 was passed.

nindian-polity-1-23.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Councils Act, 1909:
1. It associated Indians with the Viceroy's Executive Council for the first time.
2. It associated Indians with the Governors' Executive Councils for the first time.
3. S.P. Sinha became the first Indian Law Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-1-23.x: All three are correct: the 1909 Act first brought Indians into the Viceroy's and Governors' Executive Councils, and S.P. Sinha became the first Indian Law Member.

nindian-polity-1-25.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It made the Central Legislature bicameral for the first time.
2. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
3. It used the term 'responsible government' for the first time.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-1-25.x: All three are correct: the 1919 Act made the Central Legislature bicameral, introduced provincial dyarchy and first used the term 'responsible government'.

nindian-polity-1-41.s: Regarding the Chamber of Princes, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Created under – Government of India Act, 1935
First Chancellor – Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner
Created under – Government of India Act, 1919
nindian-polity-1-41.x: The Chamber of Princes, with 120 members, was created under the Government of India Act, 1919, not 1935; its first Chancellor was Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner.

nindian-polity-38-22.s:
Consider the following statements about provincial dyarchy under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It was introduced in the provinces by this Act.
2. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor and Executive Council.
3. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor and popular Ministers.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-38-22.x: All three are correct: the 1919 Act brought provincial dyarchy, with reserved subjects under the Governor and Executive Council and transferred subjects under the Governor and Ministers.

n28fe9c75572.s:
The Government of India Act, 1935 contained:
1. 321 sections
2. 14 parts
3. 10 schedules
Which of the above is/are correct?
n28fe9c75572.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 had 321 sections, 14 parts and 10 schedules.

n350222ac172.s:
Which of the following territorial changes were associated with the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Separation of Burma from India
2. Separation of Sindh from Bombay
3. Separation of Orissa from Bihar
Which of the above are correct?
n350222ac172.x: The 1935 Act provided for the separation of Burma from India, Sindh from Bombay and Orissa from Bihar.

nindian-polity-22-33.s:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
1. It proposed an All-India Federation and a Central Dyarchy.
2. Neither the All-India Federation nor the Central Dyarchy was implemented.
3. It is the model for the President's ordinance power under Article 123.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-22-33.x: All three are correct: the Federation and Central Dyarchy were proposed but never implemented, and the Act's Section 42 is the model for Article 123.

nindian-polity-22-34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It ended British sovereignty over India.
2. It gave the Constituent Assemblies both constitution-making and legislative powers.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-22-34.x: The Act ended British sovereignty and gave the Constituent Assemblies dual constitution-making and legislative powers.

nindian-polity-5-10.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Cripps Mission (1942) made the final proposal for an elected Constituent Assembly.
2. The Constituent Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-5-10.x: The Cripps Mission of 1942 proposed an elected Constituent Assembly, and the Assembly was actually constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.

nindian-polity-5-8.s:
Consider the following statements about B.N. Rau:
1. He was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly.
2. He prepared the first draft, containing 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-5-8.x: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor and prepared the first draft of 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.

na84a41d3336.s: Members of the Constituent Assembly from the provinces were:
o: Indirectly elected by Provincial Assembly members by proportional representation (single transferable vote)
na84a41d3336.x: Each community's members in the Provincial Assembly elected their representatives by proportional representation with single transferable vote; there was no adult franchise.

n7781e5dc44b.s: Sir B.N. Rau, who prepared the initial draft of the Constitution, later served as a judge of the:
n7781e5dc44b.x: B.N. Rau prepared the initial draft and later served as a judge of the International Court of Justice.

nindian-polity-1-31.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. Dr Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary President of its first meeting.
2. Dr Rajendra Prasad became its permanent President on 11 December 1946.
3. H.C. Mukherjee was its first permanent Vice-President.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-1-31.x: All three are correct: Sinha presided temporarily, Prasad became permanent President on 11 December 1946 and H.C. Mukherjee was the first permanent Vice-President.

nindian-polity-5-11.s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly election of 1946:
1. The Congress won 208 seats.
2. The Muslim League won 73 seats.
3. The Assembly was not elected on adult franchise.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-5-11.x: All three are correct: Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 (others 15), and the Assembly was not based on adult franchise.

n480de799f99.s: Which of the following is true of both the Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee?
o: Both accepted linguistic reorganisation without qualification
Both rejected linguistic States for the time being
Both recommended the immediate creation of Andhra State
Both dealt only with state boundaries
n480de799f99.x: Both turned down linguistic States at that stage, though the JVP Committee left room for Andhra if public demand was strong.

nindian-polity-5-22.s: Which of the following committee – chairman pairs is correctly matched?
o: Order of Business Committee – H.C. Mukherjee
nindian-polity-5-22.x: Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee; H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee, Nehru the States Committee and Munshi the Order of Business Committee.

nindian-polity-52-28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was chaired by Sardar Patel.
2. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Patel.
3. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by H.C. Mukherjee.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nindian-polity-52-28.x: Patel chaired both the Advisory Committee and the Provincial Constitution Committee; the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by J.B. Kripalani.

nc27e4ebc6c8.s: The Draft Constitution had 315 Articles. How many Articles did the Constitution contain as adopted?
nc27e4ebc6c8.x: The Draft had 315 Articles; the Constitution as adopted had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

n086a6d66967.s: In the Interim Government, Sardar Patel held the portfolio of:
n086a6d66967.x: Patel held Home, Information and Broadcasting; Nehru had External Affairs, Liaquat Ali Khan Finance and Rajendra Prasad Food and Agriculture.
